darwin.initialize: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{"tools":{}},"serverInfo":{"name":"nodus","version":"9.9.9"},"instructions":"Nodus is the board of Claude Code sessions the user runs this session from. Besides the session cards, it holds sticky notes and views. When the user asks you to put something on the board, or to make notes of it, write it with create_note. Read the notes they have put up with list_notes. Only write notes when the user asks for them. When the user asks for a view, a dashboard, a table, a chart or other custom UI on the board, build it with create_view; list_views, get_view and update_view find and change the views there. To put a note on another project’s board, or read the notes there, pass that project to the note tools; list_projects lists the projects. When the user asks for a new project, add it with create_project. When the user asks you to archive yourself, use archive_self. The board also holds shapes (boxes, ellipses, diamonds, words and emoji stickers) and links, arrows between cards, notes, views and shapes. The user links cards to show how their work relates: list_board shows what is on the board and where, and what this session’s card is linked to. When the user asks for something drawn, laid out, rearranged or linked on the board, use draw_on_board, update_drawing and erase_from_board. The user reads this session as a chat, which can show more than text. To show a chart, stats, a table or a text layout, call show_visual (or put the same JSON in a ```visual block in your reply). To ask the user questions with choices, call ask (or use a ```questions block), then end your turn: the answers arrive as their next message. For a mockup, a side-by-side comparison or a small tool that needs HTML, call show_page, which puts a page on the board beside your card. Prefer show_visual and ask, and don't repeat in words what they show."}}
